title: Filtered global Hom comparison for an exact adjunction with invertible derived unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian, def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive exact functor with an additive right adjoint $R$. Take complexes, their localizations, and Hom groups in a common larger universe. Let $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $D^+(\mathcal B)$ denote the localizations of bounded-below cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose the unit of the derived adjunction $L\dashv \mathbf R R$ is an isomorphism $K\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathbf R R)(LK)$ for every $K\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, where $\mathbf R R$ denotes the right derived functor of $R$, computed on bounded-below injective resolutions.
For $\mathcal E=\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, write $DF^b(\mathcal E)$ for the localization of bounded cochain complexes with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps which are quasi-isomorphisms on every grade. Filtrations are uniformly finite: $F^aP=P$ and $F^{b+1}P=0$ for integers $a\le b$ independent of cochain degree. Use the analogous bounded-below category $DF^+(\mathbf{Ab})$, and the filtered global derived Hom $R\operatorname{Hom}^F_{\mathcal E}$, forgetful functor $\omega$, filtration truncation $t^{\ge0}$, and graded functors of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus]. Exact termwise application of $L$ induces $L^F:DF^b(\mathcal A)\to DF^b(\mathcal B)$.
For $P,Q\in DF^b(\mathcal A)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism in $DF^+(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$c_{P,Q}:R\operatorname{Hom}^F_{\mathcal A}(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}^F_{\mathcal B}(L^FP,L^FQ).$$
Its underlying map is the ordinary derived Hom comparison induced by $L$ and the derived adjunction unit. Under the graded Hom formulas, $\operatorname{gr}^r c_{P,Q}$ is the finite direct sum, over $q-p=r$, of the ordinary derived Hom comparisons for $\operatorname{gr}^pP,\operatorname{gr}^qQ$. Under the canonical $H^0(\omega t^{\ge0})$ descriptions of filtered morphisms, $c_{P,Q}$ induces the map on morphisms given by $L^F$. It commutes both with the inclusion $\omega t^{\ge0}H\to\omega H$ defining the forgetful Hom map and with the projection to $H^0(\operatorname{gr}^0H)$ defining the graded morphisms.

proof.text: Choose bounded filtered representatives P and Q in the common finite filtration interval. Resolve the filtered complex L^FQ in the bounded-below filtered category by a filtered quasi-isomorphism L^FQ -> J with J termwise filtered injective, using the filtered-injective model. Thus every graded complex gr^p J is a bounded-below complex of injectives and represents L(gr^p Q).

The right adjoint R sends injectives of B to injectives of A. Indeed, for a monomorphism M -> N and a map M -> RJ, transpose the latter by L adjunction to a map LM -> J. Exactness of L makes LM -> LN a monomorphism, so injectivity of J extends the transposed map to LN -> J; transposing back gives the required extension N -> RJ. The same argument applies degreewise to the graded terms.

Write i:L^FQ -> J for the resolution from Step 1 and eta for the ordinary adjunction unit. Give RJ the termwise filtration F^p(RJ)=R(F^pJ), included in RJ by R of the inclusion. These are subobjects: if R(m)u=R(m)v for a monomorphism m, adjunction transposes this to m times the transposes of u and v being equal, so u=v. Naturality of eta and the filteredness of i show that alpha=R(i) eta_Q:Q -> RJ preserves filtration. For each term of J, [lem-trf-injective-graded-filtration-splits] splits every sequence 0 -> F^{p+1}J -> F^pJ -> gr^p J -> 0. Applying additive R preserves these split sequences, so the canonical quotient comparison gr^p(RJ) -> R(gr^p J) is an isomorphism, natural for filtered maps and hence compatible with the differentials. By Step 2 its terms are injective. Under this comparison gr^p(alpha) is R(gr^p i) eta_{gr^p Q}, the chain representative of the derived unit at gr^p Q, since exactness of L identifies gr^p(L^FQ) with L(gr^p Q) and gr^p J is a bounded-below injective representative of that object. The assumed invertibility of the derived unit therefore makes every gr^p(alpha) a quasi-isomorphism. Thus alpha is a filtered quasi-isomorphism to the bounded-below termwise filtered-injective complex RJ. Additivity gives R(0)=0, so its filtration stays in the same finite interval.

source.place: §5.1.5, derived-unit argument on associated graded resolutions

proof.text: For bounded P, form the shift-filtered Hom complexes C_A(P,RJ) and C_B(L^FP,J) of [lem-trf-filtered-hom-complex-invariance]. Their degree-n terms are finite sums of termwise Hom groups and their differentials are d f - (-1)^n f d. If epsilon is the ordinary counit, the termwise adjunction sends f:P^i -> RJ^j to epsilon_{J^j} L(f):LP^i -> J^j. Additivity and naturality in both arguments make these bijections commute with the Hom differentials. They preserve the shift filtration in both directions. Indeed the restriction of f to F^aP factors through R(F^{a+r}J) if and only if its adjoint, restricted to L(F^aP), factors through F^{a+r}J, by the adjunction bijection for F^aP and F^{a+r}J and its naturality with respect to both inclusions. Exactness of L identifies L(F^aP) with F^a(LP). Consequently we have an isomorphism of uniformly finite filtered complexes. It is natural for filtered chain maps of P and J; naturality in the localized Q follows in Step 5.

Compute RHom^F_A(P,Q) using alpha:Q -> RJ from Step 3 and RHom^F_B(L^FP,L^FQ) using i:L^FQ -> J from Step 1. The chain isomorphism of Step 4 defines c_{P,Q}. The filtered-injective localization model identifies any two such target representatives by filtered homotopy equivalences, and [lem-trf-filtered-hom-complex-invariance] sends these to filtered homotopy equivalences of Hom complexes; the same lemma inverts filtered quasi-isomorphisms between bounded sources. Together with the bifunctor and model identifications of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus], the natural chain adjunction therefore descends to the asserted canonical natural isomorphism. Forgetting the filtration gives precisely ordinary derived adjunction using the derived-unit representative alpha. Taking the canonical associated-graded Hom maps gives the sum, over q-p=r, of the ordinary adjunction comparisons, because gr^q(RJ)=R(gr^q J) is the canonical quotient comparison of Step 3 and the adjunction respects the inclusion and quotient maps. The graded formula of the calculus identifies their targets with the stated ordinary derived Hom objects.
For the map on filtered morphisms, represent a morphism by a filtered chain map f:P -> RJ. Its adjoint is epsilon_J L(f):L^FP -> J. Naturality of epsilon and the adjunction triangle identity give epsilon_J L(alpha)=epsilon_J L(R(i)) L(eta_Q)=i epsilon_{LQ} L(eta_Q)=i. Thus, in the filtered localization, epsilon_J L(f)=i (L(alpha))^{-1} L(f), which represents exactly L^F(alpha^{-1} f). This checks the claimed morphism map, rather than just its invertibility. Finally the chain isomorphism respects F^0 and F^1, and its induced squares with F^0C -> C and F^0C -> F^0C/F^1C commute. Applying H^0 and the calculus's identifications proves the forgetful and graded-projection compatibilities.
